{"kind":"proof","text":"Since \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb{R}\) and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, the inverse image \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). But
\[
Z(f)=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=f^{-1}(\{0\}).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed.","reason":"The proof uses the defining closed-set characterization of continuity; the supplied group-theoretic rule candidates are irrelevant."}
